day_shape: Israel-Lebanon trilateral talks in Washington yield agreed ceasefire renewal with 'pilot' Hezbollah-free zones, US House passes Iran war-powers resolution 215-208, UNIFIL peacekeeper killed by mortar in south Lebanon, heavy Khamenei-office messaging cycle around Imam Khomeini anniversary and Eid al-Ghadir.

threads.label: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire renewal talks
threads.summary: The US State Department announced that a fourth high-level US-Israel-Lebanon trilateral on June 2-3 produced agreement on implementing a ceasefire, with reporting of 'pilot' zones banning Hezbollah and continued Israeli freedom of action. Defence Minister Katz said Israel would continue operations in southern Lebanon, and the IDF issued its first evacuation warning south of the Zahrani River since Trump's ceasefire announcement.

threads.label: South Lebanon strikes, UNIFIL death, drones
threads.summary: UNIFIL said one peacekeeper was killed and two wounded by mortar fire near Marjayoun overnight, while the IDF reported a tank-drone operation near Beaufort, a nighttime raid on a Hezbollah weapons store, and a Hezbollah FPV drone strike weeks ago near IDF Northern Command chief Maj. Gen. Rafi Milo. Israel said it was deploying new countermeasures to Hezbollah fibre-optic and night-vision drones, and a Hezbollah official threatened Haifa and Tel Aviv if strikes on Beirut resume.

threads.label: US House Iran war-powers vote
threads.summary: The US House passed a resolution seeking to curb President Trump's Iran war powers by 215 to 208, with four Republicans joining Democrats. Defa Press and Times of Israel reported the vote as symbolic without Senate approval; Trump separately said US-Iran talks were going well and could yield a deal by the weekend, while Tehran denied progress.

threads.label: US-Iran nuclear/MOU talks stalled
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported negotiations had reached a stalemate, with Tehran insisting frozen Iranian assets be released in the first phase of any MOU. Defa Press quoted Foreign Minister Araghchi saying no tangible progress had been achieved and warning Iran's armed forces were ready to resume war and strike targets inside Israel if attacks on Beirut continue.

threads.label: Khamenei Khomeini-anniversary messaging cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office and IRIB ran an extended cycle of posts releasing the new leader Ayatollah Sayyed Mojtaba Khamenei's message for Eid al-Ghadir and the 37th anniversary of Khomeini's death, read at the shrine by Hojjatoleslam Ali Akbari. Messaging claimed the 'Zionist regime' has been militarily humiliated and that countries are diverging from it, framing the school of Khamenei as a continuation of Khomeini's.

threads.label: Iraqi militia disarmament push
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported Iraq's new Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met leaders of Iranian-linked militias and urged them to disarm and place weapons under state control. IRIB separately reported the death in Baghdad of senior Najaf-based Shia marja Ayatollah Mohammad Ishaq Fayyad at 96.

threads.label: Iran domestic and humanitarian
threads.summary: WHO announced a US$2 million emergency project with Iran's Ministry of Health to prevent disease outbreaks and sustain essential services amid multiple crises affecting public health infrastructure. Iran International reported citizen messages describing the continued use of children at security checkpoints and in military-themed programmes.

events.title: An explosive-laden first-person view (FPV) drone launched by Hezbollah struck near IDF Northern Command chief Maj. Gen. Rafi Milo, who was visiting southern Lebanon several weeks ago, according to the military. The IDF says that "no damage was caused and there were no casualties" in the incident, although reports indicate that the drone hit one of the vehicles in Milo's convoy shortly after he exited his car. Since the incident, the IDF has changed its protocols for visits of officers to southern Lebanon.

"The fighting in southern Lebanon is ongoing, as the IDF continues to target Hezbollah facilities and infrastructure located in and near your villages," warns army spokesman Col. Avichay Adraee.

He warns residents of southern Lebanon not to travel south of the Zahrani River "until further notice.
